messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test sets up:
  - It defines an option with short name 'd' and long name "debug" via OptionBuilder.withLongOpt("debug").create('d').
  - It parses the command line ["-d", "true"].
  - It asserts that commandLine.hasOption("debug") is true.

- Observed behavior tied to code:
  - CommandLine.hasOption(String) is implemented as:
    - return options.containsKey(opt);
    - This means it only returns true if the internal options map contains a key exactly equal to the string passed in.
  - The internal map is populated with Option objects keyed by Option.getKey().
  - Option.getKey() returns the short opt if present, otherwise the long opt:
    - if (opt == null) return longOpt; else return opt;
    - For the test’s Option, both opt ('d') and longOpt ("debug") are set, so getKey() returns "d".

- How the bug occurs:
  - During parsing, the selected option is added to CommandLine keyed under "d" (the short name) because Option.getKey() prefers the short name when present.
  - Later, hasOption("debug") looks up the key "debug" in the map. Since the option was stored under "d", the lookup fails and returns false.
  - This also explains the issue report: commandLine.getOptionValue("debug") returns null while getOptionValue('d') works, because the internal storage is keyed only by the short name.

- Why this contradicts documentation/expectations:
  - Users expect to be able to query options by either their short or long name, especially when they provided a long option via withLongOpt and the docs suggest this is supported.
  - The current design of CommandLine (keyed only by the short name when both exist) causes lookups by the long name to fail.

- Conclusion:
  - The root cause is that CommandLine stores options using only Option.getKey(), which returns the short option when available. Consequently, hasOption(String) and getOptionValue(String) fail for long names if a short name exists. The fix should allow lookups by both short and long names, e.g., by also storing entries keyed by longOpt, or by enhancing lookup methods to check both names.
